newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Thomson Bankwatch downgrades Romania's Bankcoop.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Bankwatch downgrades Romania's Bankcoop.

text.p: Banking credit rating service Thomson BankWatch said on Wednesday it had downgraded to LC-4 from LC-3 the short-term local currency debt rating for Romanian private bank Bankcoop.
"There have been a number of developments which reflect negatively on our rating," Thomson BankWatch president Ramin Habibi said in a statement made available to Reuters.
Bankcoop officials were not immediately available for comment.

In January, Banca de Credit Cooperatist Bankcoop SA was at the centre of a tit-for-tat between the bank's former president Alexandru Dinulescu and its main shareholder George Paunescu, head of a large media and tourism holding.
The row initially led to short-lived panic by depositors to withdraw their money, which subsided quickly.

Police arrested Dinulescu last month over bribe-taking charges one day after he resigned following the central bank's dismissal of his allegations that Paunescu's $10 million capital injection into Bankcoop had been illegal.
Bankcoop vice-president Viorel Olteanu took over the president's duties pending a shareholders' meeting later this month to elect a new president.
Thomson BankWatch said the future leadership of Bankcoop "could have a strong impact on the direction of the bank".
Bankcoop reported an end-1996 provisional balance sheet of 2.1 trillion lei, 870 billion lei up from 1995 and a 1996 gross profit of 66 billion. ($=7,744 lei)
